# `silk/crypto/ml_dsa`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Sign and verify with ML-DSA (FIPS 204), the module-lattice signature scheme, at the levels
ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, and ML-DSA-87.

## When to use
Use [`MlDsa`](#MlDsa) for signatures that must hold also against an attacker with a large quantum
computer. Make a key pair with [`MlDsa.keyPairFromSeed`](#MlDsa.impl.keyPairFromSeed), sign with [`MlDsa.sign`](#MlDsa.impl.sign), and verify
with [`MlDsa.verify`](#MlDsa.impl.verify). Use `silk.crypto.ml_key` to read and write the keys in PKCS #8 and
SubjectPublicKeyInfo.

## Details
This is the pure ML-DSA of FIPS 204 section 5, with a context string of up to 255 bytes. A key
pair comes from a 32-byte seed, the form that PKCS #8 stores; the functions of
[`MlDsaParameters`](#MlDsaParameters) give the sizes. [`MlDsa.sign`](#MlDsa.impl.sign) is the hedged variant, with 32 bytes from the
ambient `Random`, and [`MlDsa.signDeterministic`](#MlDsa.impl.signDeterministic) the deterministic one. The external-mu
functions take the 64-byte message representative mu that [`MlDsa.externalMu`](#MlDsa.impl.externalMu) computes, so a
caller can hash a long message elsewhere. The caller gives every buffer, so nothing allocates.
Signing does not branch on secret values except in the rejection loop of FIPS 204, whose
rejected attempts reveal nothing.

## Errors
- [`MlDsaError`](#MlDsaError) for a buffer of the wrong length, a context over 255 bytes, or a private key
  whose secret vectors are out of range.

## Gotchas
The verifiers return `false` for every failure, including wrong lengths. Secrets are not
erased. The pre-hash variant HashML-DSA is not here.

## Examples
### Sign and verify
```silk
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.crypto.ml_dsa { MlDsa, MlDsaError, MlDsaParameters }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let parameters = MlDsaParameters.MlDsa44
  // Real programs fill the seed from a secure `Random` provider.
  let seed: [u8; 32] = [1; 32]
  let mut publicKey: [u8; 1312] = [0; 1312]
  let mut privateKey: [u8; 2560] = [0; 2560]
  match MlDsa.keyPairFromSeed(parameters, &seed, &mut publicKey, &mut privateKey) {
    Result<(), MlDsaError>.Success { .. } => {}
    Result<(), MlDsaError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  let mut signature: [u8; 2420] = [0; 2420]
  match MlDsa.signDeterministic(parameters, &privateKey, b"hello", b"", &mut signature) {
    Result<(), MlDsaError>.Success { .. } => {}
    Result<(), MlDsaError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  if !MlDsa.verify(parameters, &publicKey, b"hello", b"", &signature) {
    return 1
  }
  if MlDsa.verify(parameters, &publicKey, b"hullo", b"", &signature) {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `MlDsa` with `import silk.crypto.ml_dsa { MlDsa }`.

<a id="MlDsa"></a>

## `MlDsa`

```silk
pub struct MlDsa
```

The functions of ML-DSA.

### When to use
Make a key pair with [`MlDsa.keyPairFromSeed`](#MlDsa.impl.keyPairFromSeed), sign with [`MlDsa.sign`](#MlDsa.impl.sign) or
[`MlDsa.signDeterministic`](#MlDsa.impl.signDeterministic), and verify with [`MlDsa.verify`](#MlDsa.impl.verify).

### Details
Each function takes the parameter set and the caller's buffers, which must have the lengths of
[`MlDsaParameters`](#MlDsaParameters).

<a id="MlDsa.impl.keyPairFromSeed"></a>

### Associated function `keyPairFromSeed`

```silk
pub fn keyPairFromSeed(
    parameters: MlDsaParameters,
    seed: &[u8],
    publicKey: &mut [u8],
    privateKey: &mut [u8],
  ) -> Result<(), MlDsaError>
```

Writes the key pair of ML-DSA.KeyGen_internal for the 32-byte `seed` into `publicKey` and
`privateKey`.

#### Errors
- `InvalidLength` if `seed` is not 32 bytes, or a key buffer does not have the length of the
  parameter set. The buffers do not change.

<a id="MlDsa.impl.generateSeed"></a>

### Associated function `generateSeed`

```silk
pub effect fn generateSeed() -> [u8; 32] ? &mut Random
```

Returns a new 32-byte seed from the ambient `Random`, for [`MlDsa.keyPairFromSeed`](#MlDsa.impl.keyPairFromSeed).

The `Random` provider must be cryptographically secure.

<a id="MlDsa.impl.externalMu"></a>

### Associated function `externalMu`

```silk
pub fn externalMu(parameters: MlDsaParameters, publicKey: &[u8], message: &[u8], context: &[u8]) -> Result<
    [u8; 64],
    MlDsaError,
  >
```

Returns mu, the 64-byte message representative of FIPS 204 for `message` and `context`
under `publicKey`, for the external-mu functions.

#### Errors
- `InvalidLength` if `publicKey` does not have the length of the parameter set.
- `ContextTooLong` if `context` is longer than 255 bytes.

<a id="MlDsa.impl.sign"></a>

### Associated function `sign`

```silk
pub effect fn sign(
    parameters: MlDsaParameters,
    privateKey: &[u8],
    message: &[u8],
    context: &[u8],
    signature: &mut [u8],
  ) -> Result<(), MlDsaError> ? &mut Random
```

Writes a hedged signature of `message` with `context` into `signature`, with 32 bytes from
the ambient `Random`.

#### Errors
- `InvalidLength` if `privateKey` or `signature` does not have the length of the parameter
  set.
- `ContextTooLong` if `context` is longer than 255 bytes.
- `InvalidPrivateKey` if the secret vectors are out of range.

<a id="MlDsa.impl.signDeterministic"></a>

```silk
  ) -> Result<(), MlDsaError>
```

Writes the deterministic signature of `message` with `context` into `signature`: FIPS 204
with 32 zero bytes as the randomness.

#### Errors
The errors of [`MlDsa.sign`](#MlDsa.impl.sign).

<a id="MlDsa.impl.signExternalMu"></a>

### Associated function `signExternalMu`

```silk
pub fn signExternalMu(
    parameters: MlDsaParameters,
    privateKey: &[u8],
    mu: &[u8],
    randomness: &[u8],
    signature: &mut [u8],
  ) -> Result<(), MlDsaError>
```

Writes the signature of ML-DSA.Sign_internal for the 64-byte message representative `mu`
and the 32-byte `randomness` into `signature`.

#### Errors
- `InvalidLength` for a key, mu, randomness, or signature buffer of the wrong length.
- `InvalidPrivateKey` if the secret vectors are out of range.

#### Gotchas
Use 32 fresh random bytes, or 32 zero bytes for the deterministic variant. Get `mu` from
[`MlDsa.externalMu`](#MlDsa.impl.externalMu) with the public key of `privateKey`.

<a id="MlDsa.impl.verify"></a>

### Associated function `verify`

```silk
pub fn verify(
    parameters: MlDsaParameters,
    publicKey: &[u8],
    message: &[u8],
    context: &[u8],
    signature: &[u8],
  ) -> bool
```

Returns whether `signature` is a valid signature of `message` with `context` under
`publicKey`. Wrong lengths and a context over 255 bytes give `false`.

<a id="MlDsa.impl.verifyExternalMu"></a>

### Associated function `verifyExternalMu`

```silk
pub fn verifyExternalMu(parameters: MlDsaParameters, publicKey: &[u8], mu: &[u8], signature: &[u8]) -> bool
```

Returns whether `signature` is valid under `publicKey` for the 64-byte message
representative `mu`, as ML-DSA.Verify_internal checks it. Wrong lengths give `false`.
